proposals: DGTR should show, on each active investigation’s case page, the statutory deadline for final findings and the current procedural stage, so trackers can read the TPA and dyes decision dates from the regulator rather than guessing at “any week in Aug–Sep 2026”.

DGTR should publish a single downloadable list of all initiated and ongoing investigations with the HSN codes covered, so a lead such as the ANTU case can be confirmed or ruled out in minutes instead of sitting in a tracker as “unconfirmed”.

BIS and the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should publish a consolidated register of chemical Quality Control Orders with HSN codes, notification dates and enforcement status, so a QCO is never mistaken for a trade-remedy case or carried with a guessed code.

The Ministry of Environment should display, on PARIVESH, the current stage and expected decision date of each Environmental Clearance proposal, including BPCL’s Andhra Pradesh project, so a ₹1,45,000 crore project’s clearance status is not known only through a CMD’s remarks to a Chief Minister.

Jharkhand IIDCL and Tamil Nadu SIPCOT should publish monthly land-acquisition progress for the BHAVYA dye parks, in acres and per cent of requirement, so the 60% and 40% figures can be tracked against the FY28–29 operationalisation target from a primary source.
